hardware_review: The same overhead dock and finite pin mechanism retained capture and stayed within pin/contact/service checks in both failed runs. No geometry or acceptance-limit change is proposed. a42 used equivalent physical geometry but a different source hash and also remains a failed reference.
diagnosis: a45 failed during transport before its changed goal handoff. Shared legacy controller/policy hashes match a43, but floating-point trajectories diverged; a43 reaching the goal therefore does not establish robust transport. At a45 termination the pursuit controller still requested turning toward the path heading while measured ropes pointed significantly behind/right in body coordinates.
change: Use measured outgoing rope direction as body yaw reference (gain 1.5, unchanged 0.2 rad/s cap and 0.10 rad/s^2 slew). Preserve the existing world-frame pursuit translation, 85 N feedback, hardware, and goal handoff correction.
hypothesis: Reducing sideways pull on the rear receiver may reduce yaw/stance conflict; this is not yet a causal or feasibility proof.
limits: All physical acceptance limits unchanged; no external forces, state writes, collision masking or foot-contact resets.
